cases.sentence: ___ и строгое выражение лица пугали ее.
options: глаза
глаз
глазам
глазами
cases.explain: Глаза is part of the compound grammatical subject of пугали (frightened), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Он знает, какого мучения ей стоит всякое воспоминание о нем, и, зная ее, требует от нее ___.
options: письмо
письма
письму
письмом
cases.explain: The verb требовать (to demand) governs the genitive case for its object, giving письма.

cases.sentence: «Моя дочь по ___ не моя дочь, а Каренина.
options: закон
закона
закону
законом
cases.explain: The preposition по (according to) governs the dative case, giving закону.

cases.sentence: Дарья Александровна села на садовую ___ в углу аллеи.
options: скамейка
скамейки
скамейку
скамейкой
cases.explain: The preposition на (onto) with a verb of placement governs the accusative case, giving скамейку.

cases.sentence: Мы соединены самыми святыми для нас ___ любви.
options: узы
уз
узам
узами
cases.explain: Узами is the instrumental case, expressing the means by which they are joined (соединены узами).

cases.sentence: Нельзя представить себе моральных мучений хуже тех, которые она пережила в две недели в ___.
options: Петербург
Петербурга
Петербургу
Петербурге
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) indicating location governs the prepositional case, giving Петербурге.

reading.ru: Нет, я думаю, княгиня устала, и лошади ее не интересуют, сказал Вронский Анне, предложившей пройти до конного завода, где Свияжский хотел видеть нового жеребца.
reading.question: Why did Vronsky suggest Dolly not go to the stud farm?
options: He thought the princess was tired and not interested in horses
He wanted to keep Sviyazhsky company alone
He was afraid the new stallion was dangerous
He wanted Anna to go instead
reading.correct: He thought the princess was tired and not interested in horses
reading.explain: Vronsky tells Anna he thinks the princess is tired and not interested in horses.

reading.ru: Он снял шляпу и, достав платок, отер им свою плешивевшую голову.
reading.question: What did Vronsky do with his hat and handkerchief?
options: He took off his hat and wiped his balding head with a handkerchief
He threw his hat on the ground in anger
He offered his handkerchief to Dolly
He fanned himself with his hat
reading.correct: He took off his hat and wiped his balding head with a handkerchief
reading.explain: The text says he took off his hat and, taking out a handkerchief, wiped his balding head with it.

reading.question: What does Vronsky ask of Dolly early in their private conversation?
options: To help him
To leave immediately
To speak to Anna about her health
To write a letter for him
reading.explain: Vronsky simply says, "Help me," appealing directly to Dolly.

reading.ru: Никто больше и сильнее меня не чувствует всей тяжести положения Анны.
reading.question: What does Vronsky claim about how deeply he feels Anna's situation?
options: That no one feels the weight of Anna's situation more than he does
That he does not really understand Anna's situation
That Dolly feels it more than he does
That Anna herself does not feel it at all
reading.correct: That no one feels the weight of Anna's situation more than he does
reading.explain: Vronsky states that no one feels the full weight of Anna's position more strongly than he does.

reading.ru: «В свете это ад», — мрачно нахмурившись, быстро проговорил он.
reading.question: How does Vronsky describe society's treatment of Anna and himself?
options: He calls it hell
He calls it comfortable
He calls it fair
He calls it boring
reading.explain: Vronsky says, frowning gloomily, that in society it is hell for them.

reading.ru: «Я знаю, что она ожила после всех ее страданий.
reading.question: What does Vronsky say about Anna after her past suffering?
options: That she has come back to life after all her suffering
That she is still deeply depressed
That she has forgotten her past entirely
That she wants to return to Petersburg
reading.correct: That she has come back to life after all her suffering
reading.explain: Vronsky says he knows Anna has revived after all her suffering.

reading.ru: Дарья Александровна села на садовую скамейку в углу аллеи.
reading.question: Where did Dolly sit while listening to Vronsky?
options: On a garden bench in the corner of the avenue
On the grass under a tree
On the terrace steps
Inside the house by the window
reading.correct: On a garden bench in the corner of the avenue
reading.explain: The text says Darya Alexandrovna sat down on a garden bench in the corner of the avenue.

reading.ru: Но жребий брошен, — сказал он, переходя с русского на французский язык.
reading.question: What did Vronsky say as he switched from Russian to French?
options: That the die is cast
That he regrets everything
That he wants to leave Anna
That nothing has been decided yet
reading.explain: Vronsky says the die is cast, switching to French as he speaks.

reading.ru: «Моя дочь по закону не моя дочь, а Каренина.
reading.question: What legal problem does Vronsky describe about his daughter?
options: By law she is not his daughter but a Karenina
She has no birth certificate at all
She is legally considered an orphan
She cannot be baptized
reading.correct: By law she is not his daughter but a Karenina
reading.explain: Vronsky says that legally his daughter is not his daughter, but a Karenina, since Anna is still married to Karenin.

reading.ru: И завтра родится сын, мой сын, и он по закону Каренин.
reading.question: What future problem does Vronsky anticipate regarding a possible son?
options: That any son born would legally be a Karenin, not his heir
That he does not want any more children
That a son would be sent away to boarding school
That Karenin would refuse to acknowledge the child at all
reading.correct: That any son born would legally be a Karenin, not his heir
reading.explain: Vronsky says that if a son is born tomorrow, he would legally be a Karenin, not his own heir.

reading.ru: Я счастлив ее любовью, но я должен иметь занятие.
reading.question: What does Vronsky say he needs besides Anna's love?
options: An occupation
More money
A title
Solitude
reading.explain: Vronsky says he is happy in her love, but he must have an occupation.

reading.ru: Я работаю здесь, сидя на месте, и я счастлив, доволен, и нам ничего более не нужно для счастья.
reading.question: How does Vronsky describe his current life and work in the countryside?
options: He works here, staying in one place, and is happy and content
He is restless and wants to travel constantly
He regrets settling in the countryside
He feels his work is meaningless
reading.correct: He works here, staying in one place, and is happy and content
reading.explain: Vronsky says he works here, staying put, and is happy and content, needing nothing more for happiness.

reading.ru: Главное же то, что работая, необходимо иметь убеждение, что дело мое не умрет со мною, что у меня будут наследники, а этого у меня нет.
reading.question: What does Vronsky say is essential for meaningful work, which he lacks?
options: The conviction that his work will not die with him because he will have heirs
A large salary
Public recognition
A team of assistants
reading.correct: The conviction that his work will not die with him because he will have heirs
reading.explain: Vronsky explains that what matters most is the conviction that one's work will not die with oneself because there will be heirs, which he lacks.

reading.ru: Даже для того, чтобы просить государя об усыновлении, необходим развод.
reading.question: Why does Vronsky say a divorce is necessary?
options: Even to petition the tsar for the child's legitimation, a divorce is required
To allow Anna to remarry someone else
To let Vronsky inherit his father's estate
To register the hospital officially
reading.correct: Even to petition the tsar for the child's legitimation, a divorce is required
reading.explain: Vronsky explains that even to ask the sovereign to legitimize the child, a divorce is necessary.

reading.ru: «Разумеется, — сказал он мрачно, — это одна из тех фарисейских жестокостей, на которые способны только эти люди без сердца».
reading.question: How does Vronsky characterize Karenin's circle for demanding a letter from Anna?
options: As capable of Pharisaical cruelties, being people without heart
As kind and understanding
As simply following the law without malice
As eager to help Anna
reading.correct: As capable of Pharisaical cruelties, being people without heart
reading.explain: Vronsky gloomily calls it one of the Pharisaical cruelties only heartless people are capable of.

reading.ru: — Так вот, княгиня, я за вас бессовестно хватаюсь, как за якорь спасения.
reading.question: How does Vronsky describe his reliance on Dolly's help?
options: He shamelessly clings to her as an anchor of salvation
He says he does not need her help at all
He compares her to a distant relative
He says he would rather ask Sviyazhsky
reading.correct: He shamelessly clings to her as an anchor of salvation
reading.explain: Vronsky says he is shamelessly clinging to her, princess, as to an anchor of salvation.

reading.ru: Сказала Дарья Александровна, вдруг почему-то при этом вспоминая странную новую привычку Анны Щурица.
reading.question: What odd new habit of Anna's did Dolly suddenly recall?
options: Anna's habit of squinting her eyes
Anna's habit of biting her nails
Anna's habit of humming softly
Anna's habit of tapping her foot
reading.correct: Anna's habit of squinting her eyes
reading.explain: Dolly suddenly recalls Anna's strange new habit of squinting, referred to in the text as her 'Щурится' habit.

reading.ru: Они встали и пошли к дому.
reading.question: What did Dolly and Vronsky do at the end of their conversation?
options: They got up and walked toward the house
They stayed on the bench until dark
They went their separate ways angrily
They went to find Anna at the stud farm
reading.correct: They got up and walked toward the house
reading.explain: The text ends the conversation with them getting up and walking toward the house.

highlight.question: Which sentence depicts the speaker removing his hat and wiping his head?
sentences: – Вы угадали, что мне хотелось поговорить с вами?
– сказал он, смеющимися глазами глядя на нее.
– Я не ошибаюсь, что вы друг Анны.
– Он снял шляпу и, достав платок, отер им свою плешивевшую голову.
highlight.explain: This sentence describes his physical gesture as he begins the conversation, taking out a handkerchief to wipe his bald head.

highlight.question: Which sentence expresses the speaker's understanding of why Darya came to visit them?
sentences: – Если вы приехали к нам, вы, единственная женщина из прежних друзей Анны, – я не считаю княжну Варвару, – то я понимаю, что вы сделали это не потому, что вы считаете наше положение нормальным, но потому, что вы, понимая всю тяжесть этого положения, все так же любите ее и хотите помочь ей.
Так ли я вас понял?
– спросил он, оглянувшись на нее.
highlight.explain: The speaker explains that she came not to approve of their situation but because she understands its gravity and still loves and wants to help Anna.

highlight.question: Which sentence suggests that the speaker may be overstating his own responsibility?
sentences: – Я понимаю, – сказала Дарья Александровна, невольно любуясь им, как он искренно и твердо сказал это.
– Но именно потому, что вы себя чувствуете причиной, вы преувеличиваете, я боюсь, – сказала она.
– Положение ее тяжело в свете, я понимаю.
highlight.explain: Darya tactfully indicates that because he feels himself the cause, he is likely exaggerating the extent of his guilt.

highlight.question: Which sentence reveals the speaker's fear about what the future holds?
sentences: – Да, да, – сказал он.
– Я знаю, что она ожила после всех ее страданий; она счастлива.
Она счастлива настоящим.
Но я?..  я боюсь того, что ожидает нас…
Виноват, вы хотите идти?
highlight.explain: He explicitly expresses his anxiety about what awaits them despite Anna's current happiness.

highlight.question: Which sentence demonstrates the speaker's pride in his work and accomplishments?
sentences: Это раздражает ее.
Она не понимает, и я не могу ей высказать все.
Теперь посмотрите с другой стороны.
Я счастлив ее любовью, но я должен иметь занятия.
Я нашел это занятие, и горжусь этим занятием, и считаю его более благородным, чем занятия моих бывших товарищей при дворе и по службе.
highlight.explain: He states that he found an occupation of which he is proud, considering it more noble than his former work at court and in government service.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes the cruel demand being made of Anna?
sentences: И теперь, я знаю, он не отказал бы.
Стоило бы только написать ему.
Он прямо отвечал тогда, что если она выразит желание, он не откажет.
Разумеется, – сказал он мрачно, – это одна из этих фарисейских жестокостей, на которые способны только эти люди без сердца.
Он знает, какого мучения ей стоит всякое воспоминание о нем, и, зная ее, требует от нее письма.
highlight.explain: The sentence explains that someone is demanding a letter from Anna despite knowing how painful any memory of him causes her suffering.
